Learn which mechanism and machine frame your next workshop needs. 01 / Your first workshop Start small. Build a kingdom. Ten connected workshops, from andesite to the Sovereign project. Build the first Kinetic Machine by hand, then automate mechanisms. The Nether opens in chapter 3, AE2 and Mekanism begin in chapter 4, and the End opens in chapter 5. 01 Andesite · Roots of Industry Mechanical power, wood, crops and geological processing Kinetic Machine 02 Copper · Fields & Fluids Copper, seals, fluids, irrigation and ocean minerals Hydraulic Machine 03 Brass · Into the Nether Nether heat, brass logistics and Hypertubes Precision Machine 04 Inductive · The Connected Workshop First FE, AE2 networks, processors and parallel arcane automation Inductive Machine 05 Ender · Beyond the Portal End access, advanced Mekanism factories and Dragon’s Breath Ender Machine 06 Reinforced · Chemical Engineering HDPE, gases, chemical equipment and ME chemical storage Chemical Machine 07 Integrated · Living Expeditions Radiance, 16k storage, airships and expeditions Expedition Frame 08 Containment · Nuclear Control Overcharge, fission, waste handling, turbines and spatial storage Containment Frame 09 Singularity · Quantum Industry Stargaze, retained Void imprint, SPS, fusion and quantum links Singularity Frame 10 Sovereign · A Renewable Kingdom Sovereign Keystone, 256k storage and advanced powered equipment Sovereign Core Your first steps Kelp + clay → Algal Blend. Andesite + blend → Andesite Alloy. Craft the first frame: 7 alloy + casing + slab (AAA / ACA / ASA). Stonecut separate frames into power, press, basin, mixer and Deployer. Sequence mechanisms and deploy them onto casings. 02 / Build your machines One frame, a choice of machines Each frame has a clear tier and production role. Tier Frame Assembly Workshop role 1 Kinetic Machine Andesite Casing → deploy Kinetic Mechanism Mechanical power, wood, crops and geological processing 2 Hydraulic Machine Copper Casing → deploy Sealed Mechanism Copper, seals, fluids, irrigation and ocean minerals 3 Precision Machine Brass Casing → deploy Precision Mechanism Nether heat, brass logistics and Hypertubes 4 Inductive Machine Steel Casing → deploy Inductive Mechanism First FE, AE2 networks, processors and parallel arcane automation 5 Ender Machine Steel Casing → deploy Ender Mechanism End access, advanced Mekanism factories and Dragon’s Breath 6 Chemical Machine Steel Casing → deploy Reinforced Mechanism HDPE, gases, chemical equipment and ME chemical storage 7 Expedition Frame Arcane Casing → deploy Expedition Mechanism Radiance, 16k storage, airships and expeditions 8 Containment Frame Steel Casing → deploy Containment Mechanism Overcharge, fission, waste handling, turbines and spatial storage 9 Singularity Frame Fluix Block → deploy Singularity Mechanism Stargaze, retained Void imprint, SPS, fusion and quantum links 10 Sovereign Core Sps Casing → deploy Sovereign Mechanism Sovereign Keystone, 256k storage and advanced powered equipment Chapter 4 also has a parallel Arcane Machine for Ars and Wizardry. Every mechanism uses sequenced assembly; only the first Kinetic Machine has a manual raw-material startup recipe. Stonecutting consumes its input frame. A listed batch is the result of that one recipe. 03 / Follow the chain Tier walkthroughs Exact inputs, ordered operations and reachable machine bootstraps. Andesite · Roots of Industry Mechanical power, wood, crops and geological processing. Algal Blend — Kelp + clay makes two blend by hand, four in a mixer. Start a kelp farm beside your workshop. Andesite Alloy — Andesite + blend makes two alloy by hand, four in a mixer. Original nugget alloy recipes are excluded. Build the first frame — Craft 7 alloy + slab + Andesite Casing in AAA / ACA / ASA. Cut separate frames into power, press, mixer and Deployer. This route needs no mechanism. Turn the wheel — Stonecut one frame into three wheels. Connect shafts and gears; supply water. Assemble the workshop — Stonecut a manual frame into the Deployer. Add mixer, press and basin. Keep two deployers for alloys and a third holding the ordinary hammer. Kinetic Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds betterend:iron_hammer. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Kinetic Machine — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Ordered mechanism path: Any matching Wooden Slabs → deploy Andesite Alloy → deploy Andesite Alloy → finish with Iron Hammer . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Andesite Casing → deploy Kinetic Mechanism → Kinetic Machine → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Copper · Fields & Fluids Copper, seals, fluids, irrigation and ocean minerals. Cure the rubber — Compact slime, dried kelp and 250 mB water. Mix one wheat, one kelp and 250 mB water into two slimeballs; supply the seals line. Ocean metallurgy — Mix bone meal, kelp and water into calcium powder. Compact prismarine shard, copper sheet and powder into two alloy; rods supply the Conduit Cage. Sealed Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds farmersdelight:iron_knife. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Hydraulic Machine — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Route fluids — Cut a Hydraulic Machine into a pump. Keep separate tanks for water, milk and later XP. Water the fields — Use the frame-based sprinkler recipe, then connect water. The Slicer automates supported Farmer’s Delight cutting recipes using a held knife. Ordered mechanism path: Kinetic Mechanism → deploy Copper Sheet → deploy Cured Rubber → finish with Iron Knife . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Copper Casing → deploy Sealed Mechanism → Hydraulic Machine → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Brass · Into the Nether Nether heat, brass logistics and Hypertubes. Enter the Nether — Chapter 2 unlocks Nether entry. Capture a Blaze in a burner before heated brass mixing. Heat the brass — Heat copper and zinc in the basin. Press brass sheets and finish electron tubes for the precision sequence. Build smart logistics — Precision frames supply brass sorting, mechanical crafting and automatic stocking. Link the workshop — Build the native tube sections; use precision frames for entrances and accelerators. Supply power and test a short route first. Precision Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds create:sand_paper. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Precision Machine — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Ordered mechanism path: Sealed Mechanism → deploy Brass Sheet → deploy Electron Tube → finish with Sand Paper . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Brass Casing → deploy Precision Mechanism → Precision Machine → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Inductive · The Connected Workshop First FE, AE2 networks, processors and parallel arcane automation. Bootstrap steel — Heated mixing uses two iron ingots and coal for two steel. Five steel, two osmium and one Precision Machine produce Steel Casing; no FE or boss core is required. First powered processing — Deploy a Precision Mechanism onto Steel Casing. Add Heat Generator and basic universal cables. Native infusing supplies circuits and alloys. Charge certus — Craft from Steel Casing, certus and Crafts & Additions Capacitor. Use FE to charge certus; native water conversion produces fluix crystals. Print the processors — Steel Casing + Electric Motor + gold. All four press recipes are available from this chapter; use the normal Inscriber routes. Inductive Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds betterend:iron_hammer. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Inductive Machine — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Wire a small ME network — Inductive Machine supplies the network devices. Begin with a terminal, drive, 1k cells and energy acceptor before expanding channels. Ordered mechanism path: Precision Mechanism → deploy Capacitor → deploy Fluix Crystal → finish with Iron Hammer . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Steel Casing → deploy Inductive Mechanism → Inductive Machine → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Ender · Beyond the Portal End access, advanced Mekanism factories and Dragon’s Breath. Prepare the portal — The four authored eye deployments use Inductive Mechanisms with Source Gem, pearl, Blaze Rod or crying obsidian. Other unique eyes keep native exploration sources. End Remastered still needs twelve different valid eyes. Claim the first Dragon Core — Defeat the Ender Dragon after opening the portal. Claim the permanent Dragon Core from the detected Dragon trial quest; it is retained by final imprinting. Gather chorus — Grow chorus on End Stone. Save Dragon’s Breath for Dragons Plus and the final workshop. Scale the powered workshop — Upgrade basic machines into advanced factories with their preserving native recipes. Advanced circuits become a regular supply line. Handle Dragon’s Breath — Collect bottles during the fight. Dragons Plus keeps its actual breath filling, emptying and ending fan processes; use the fluid hatch for transport. Ender Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds farmersdelight:diamond_knife. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Ender Machine — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Defeat Ender Dragon — Defeat the Ender Dragon and claim the permanent Dragon Core from this quest. Keep the core for final imprinting; it is retained. Ordered mechanism path: Inductive Mechanism → deploy Chorus Fruit → deploy Advanced Control Circuit → finish with Diamond Knife . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Steel Casing → deploy Ender Mechanism → Ender Machine → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Reinforced · Chemical Engineering HDPE, gases, chemical equipment and ME chemical storage. Grow the chemical feedstock — Farm crops → crusher Bio Fuel → PRC with water and hydrogen → substrate/ethylene. Separate water into hydrogen and oxygen; liquefy ethylene and run the second PRC recipe for HDPE. Three pellets enrich into one sheet. Forge Shadow Steel — Heat two steel, obsidian and chorus into two Shadow Steel. Press sheets; combine them with HDPE in the Reinforced Mechanism sequence. Reinforced Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds mekanismtools:steel_paxel. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Chemical Machine — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Control the gas network — Chemical Machines build advanced chemical equipment. Evaporation produces brine; separating brine gives chlorine. Infuse hydrogen + chlorine into hydrogen chloride. Store chemicals in ME — Craft the chemical housing with Chemical Machines. Combine with an AE2 component; native preserving cell upgrades keep their stored chemicals. Defeat Lich — A player kill awards the reusable core. Keep it for imprinting; repeated kills add parallel production capacity. Ordered mechanism path: Ender Mechanism → deploy Shadow Steel Sheet → deploy Hdpe Sheet → finish with Steel Paxel . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Steel Casing → deploy Reinforced Mechanism → Chemical Machine → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Integrated · Living Expeditions Radiance, 16k storage, airships and expeditions. Refine the radiance — Inject one Shadow Steel with 100 units hydrogen chloride per finished operation, then press the Refined Radiance. This is gas processing in the Chemical Injection Chamber. Expedition Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds farmersdelight:diamond_knife. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Expedition Frame — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Expand remote automation — Use 16k storage and wireless access to service the expedition workshop. Channels, energy and native wireless range still apply. Defeat The Harbinger — A player kill awards the reusable core. Keep it for imprinting; repeated kills add parallel production capacity. Ordered mechanism path: Reinforced Mechanism → deploy Manipulation Essence → deploy Radiance Sheet → finish with Diamond Knife . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Arcane Casing → deploy Expedition Mechanism → Expedition Frame → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Containment · Nuclear Control Overcharge, fission, waste handling, turbines and spatial storage. Infuse Overcharge Alloy — Infuse Refined Radiance with 80 diamond infusion units per operation. Press sheets for the Containment Mechanism; no radioactive input is needed to build the first reactor. Containment Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds create:sand_paper. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Containment Frame — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Build fission safely — Build reactor, cooling and turbine before adding fuel. Native uranium → yellow cake → uranium oxide → uranium hexafluoride → fissile fuel remains the fuel chain. Separate radioactive waste — Route waste away from normal gas storage. Use native barrels and solar neutron activation; never vent waste. Route polonium/plutonium with their native restrictions. Defeat Ignis — A player kill awards the reusable core. Keep it for imprinting; repeated kills add parallel production capacity. Ordered mechanism path: Expedition Mechanism → deploy Hdpe Sheet → deploy Overcharge Sheet → finish with Sand Paper . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Steel Casing → deploy Containment Mechanism → Containment Frame → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Singularity · Quantum Industry Stargaze, retained Void imprint, SPS, fusion and quantum links. Build the SPS line — Native waste processing and SPS produce antimatter. The native pellet recipe still costs 1000 units; there is no crafting shortcut. Nucleosynthesize a Stargaze — One AE2 Singularity + 10 antimatter units → one Stargaze Singularity in the Antiprotonic Nucleosynthesizer. Deploy a retained Void Core onto it, then use the Void-attuned Singularity with polonium for the next mechanism. Singularity Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds ars_nouveau:enchanters_sword. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Singularity Frame — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Power quantum production — Fusion requires native deuterium/tritium and ignition. SPS and quantum networks consume real energy; size the power line for sustained production. Link distant factories — 64k storage and quantum bridges support distant production while preserving AE2’s native channels and link rules. Defeat Ender Guardian — A player kill awards the reusable core. Keep it for imprinting; repeated kills add parallel production capacity. Ordered mechanism path: Containment Mechanism → deploy Pellet Polonium → deploy Void-attuned Singularity → finish with Enchanters Sword . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Fluix Block → deploy Singularity Mechanism → Singularity Frame → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. Sovereign · A Renewable Kingdom Sovereign Keystone, 256k storage and advanced powered equipment. Imprint the Sovereign Keystone — Deploy Verdant Sigil, Storm Core, Ember Core, Void Core and Dragon Core onto a Sovereign Core in one sequence. Every core is retained; finish using the ordinary Enchanter’s Sword. Sovereign Mechanism — Use the ordered sequenced assembly recipe. One loop guarantees one mechanism; the final Deployer holds betterend:diamond_hammer. Ordinary tools wear; the chapter reward version is unbreakable. Sovereign Core — Deploy this tier’s mechanism onto its listed casing. Tier 1 also has the expensive manual startup route. Stonecutting consumes a frame; each output is a separate choice. Equip the industrial kingdom — Sovereign Cores build the advanced equipment layer. Modules, energy and native upgrade components are still required. Finish the large ME network — Use native preserving upgrades to reach 256k. Storage capacity supports production; creative cells and infinity upgrades remain unavailable. Ordered mechanism path: Singularity Mechanism → deploy Pellet Antimatter → deploy Dragon Breath → finish with Diamond Hammer . One loop, one guaranteed result. Open recipe → Machine path: Sps Casing → deploy Sovereign Mechanism → Sovereign Core → the listed stonecutting, crafting, apparatus or preserving upgrade recipe. 04 / Renewable resources Stone into materials Place the selector immediately below the generated stone, and its frame one block further down. Stonecutting it gives the working Create machine you choose. A Kinetic Machine sitting in the world does not generate rotation or harvest crops. Collection: choose the right upgrade Collector Earliest point in this pack What it actually does Useful placement Vanilla Hopper Before Create Collects loose items over its opening and transfers inventory contents Under a drop point or furnace Sophisticated Hopper Upgrade Tier 1, after your first Kinetic Mechanism Pulls from the container above and pushes into the one below A vertical input → upgraded storage → output stack Sophisticated Pickup Upgrade Tier 2 Collects filtered item entities that touch the storage block At the end of a drop chute Sophisticated Magnet Upgrade Tier 3 Collects filtered nearby item entities Beside a bounded collection area Advanced Hopper / Pickup / Magnet Tier 3 Adds the corresponding advanced controls; Hopper can select sides Sorting and controlled transfers A Hopper Upgrade is not a vacuum. For loose drops in tier 1, use a vanilla hopper; for contact collection use Pickup, and for collection over an area use Magnet. Magnet range and upgrade speed depend on the installed configuration. ◆ A SIMPLE TIER 1 TRANSFER STACK Craft a Sophisticated chest or barrel with a free upgrade slot. A vanilla chest cannot accept its upgrades. Make the T&K3 Upgrade Base : two Iron Sheets, two planks and one Kinetic Mechanism, in the listed shaped pattern. Make the native Hopper Upgrade : one hopper, two iron ingots, the Upgrade Base and three redstone dust. Redstone can be mined before renewable Scoria production. Put an input inventory above the upgraded storage and an output inventory below it. Basic Hopper transfer is top → bottom. Add a vanilla hopper at the loose-item drop point if needed. Feed one item through before leaving the build running. To keep the middle container as a buffer, disable unwanted transfer or arrange the output so only the intended process receives items. At tier 3, the Advanced Hopper Upgrade can choose input and output sides. Storage and backpack upgrades are different items: use the module for your actual container. Visualise Upgrade Base · Visualise Hopper Upgrade Rotation: power before speed Use the first frame to stonecut three Water Wheels , or a different machine from its recipe. You receive that selected output, not the entire workshop. Supply the wheels with flowing water, connect shafts and add machines one at a time. RPM controls working speed; stress capacity limits how much the network can drive. Gearing for more RPM also increases the stress of many attached machines. If a network becomes overstressed, slow or disconnect a branch and add capacity before expanding it. More speed is not the solution to every bottleneck. Use a Clutch when you want to stop a branch while leaving the rest of the workshop running. Place a buffer before a slow machine. In-game Create Ponder, available by holding W over supported Create items, explains the physical placement and rotation of the native blocks. Crop farm: wheat, carrots and potatoes Tier 1. A small rotating arm is an accessible first farm. The support arm and Harvesters sit at different heights: the arm runs above the plants; the Harvesters hang at plant height. Start with vanilla crops; test unfamiliar modded crops on a short arm before planting a whole field. Parts: one Mechanical Bearing; a glued arm or chassis; Harvesters covering your chosen rows; one attached chest or barrel; rotation; and, for automatic unloading, two Portable Storage Interfaces plus a receiving hopper or funnel. Prepare a hydrated, well-lit field and plant the crop. Leave room for the arm to pass across the plants. Point the bearing upwards and attach a glued central column and support arm. Mount Harvesters underneath the arm at crop height, facing the direction in which the arm moves. Glue the storage and all moving parts into the same contraption. Keep the receiving chest and hopper stationary. Supply rotation and assemble the bearing. Moving Harvesters harvest mature crops and reset supported plants when Create's replant setting is enabled. A stationary Harvester alone is not a working farm. Put one Portable Storage Interface on the arm and another on the fixed unloading point. Their faces must align as the arm passes, with one or two air blocks between them; start with one. Extract from the stationary interface into storage. It represents the inventories on the contraption while docked. The farm pauses for exchange and then continues. Keep seeds available for expanding the field. Do not mill all wheat immediately: tier 2 slime production needs wheat itself . Slower rotation is usually sufficient while crops grow. If it fails: check hydration and light; harvester orientation and height; glue on the chest; the replant configuration; aligned interfaces; and space in the output. A full chest can stop a perfectly good unloading station. Build heights — a small bearing farm Use a three-block harvesting radius for your first test. Hydrate the field within four blocks of a water source; the bearing occupies the centre, so place water beside it. Add light and leave the sweep clear. Layer Placement Check Y = 0 — GROUND Farmland, water and the upward-facing bearing Feed the bearing from below; keep farmland hydrated Y = 1 — CROP Wheat, carrots or potatoes; moving Harvesters The Harvesters pass through the plant layer, facing the direction of travel Y = 2 — SUPPORT Glued support arm and attached inventory Hang the Harvesters underneath; connect the arm to the bearing with a glued central column ◆ FIRST TEST Start with one mature crop in the sweep. Confirm HARVEST → REPLANT → MOVING STORAGE → FIXED STORAGE before extending the field. Hold W over the Mechanical Harvester and Portable Storage Interface for Create’s placement demonstrations. Wood farm: cut, replant, reserve saplings Tier 1 equipment; easier unattended sorting at tier 3. Use oak or birch for the first test. Larger and modded trees can need different spacing, growth clearance and cutting behaviour. Parts: a Mechanical Bearing and glued arm; a Mechanical Saw for each cutting lane; Deployers for replanting; attached storage containing saplings; two interfaces for unloading; rotation; and an output buffer. Lay out dirt planting spots around the sweep. Leave enough light and air above them for trees to grow. Put moving Saws at the level of the lowest trunk block, facing into the path of the trees. The cut must disconnect the tree from the ground; cutting a higher log can leave a stump. Place Deployers to visit the cleared dirt. Their interaction target is two blocks in front of the block, at the sapling-space height above dirt. A Deployer facing downwards uses a different height offset; test the reach before gluing the arm. Set each Deployer's filter to the sapling you want. On a moving contraption, it takes matching items from the attached inventories and replants. Put an initial sapling supply in the moving storage. Check that a planted tree grows, is cut and is replanted before adding more lanes. Unload at the interface pair. Keep saplings on the contraption. In tier 1, empty logs manually for the first build, or add a vanilla sorting-and-return circuit. In tier 3, filtered brass extraction makes selective unloading much simpler. For an unattended farm, the unloading system must leave or return planting stock. Pulling every item out with an unfiltered hopper eventually empties the saplings. Set aside a reserve before sending excess saplings elsewhere, and give sticks, apples and surplus drops a destination too. Better plank yield The pack's Saw routes cover 200 verified wood pairs . Most logs follow log → stripped log → six planks . Use the Saw's output filter when the same input has several possible results; its normal recipe cycling can otherwise make different products. Bamboo blocks give three planks. Some woods have no stripped counterpart and go directly to planks. Wood recipe compatibility does not guarantee that every custom tree has vanilla growth or tree-cutting behaviour. Use the recipe catalogue for that wood's exact input and output. Check the cutting and planting layers Component Position / target First test SAW At the lowest trunk layer, one block above the dirt Cut one grown oak tree; no trunk stump should remain DEPLOYER Targets the empty sapling space above dirt, two blocks in front of its face With the farm stopped, confirm the target height and reach MOVING STORAGE Glued to the same contraption Load saplings before assembling; set the Deployer filter UNLOADING An aligned moving/fixed interface pair Export logs while retaining or returning saplings ◆ FIRST TEST Use ONE PLANTING POSITION . Watch a complete PLANT → GROW → CUT → REPLANT cycle. Check the Deployer’s two-block reach with in-game Ponder before extending the moving arm. Leave room for the tree canopy and keep planting stock out of general extraction. Kelp, sugar cane and bamboo These are good supply farms because the base plant can stay in place. Harvest the upper growth and keep the bottom plant for regrowth. Before Create: use a small manual plot, or a vanilla piston/observer design with hopper collection. Native redstone recipes remain the starting route. With Create: move a Harvester across the upper growth. For underwater kelp, keep the bottom kelp planted and provide a collection/storage path on the contraption. Sugar cane: plant next to water and leave the lowest cane. Place harvesting at the height you actually want removed. Bamboo: leave planting stock and growth room. Check the exact Saw recipe before routing bamboo blocks into planks. Kelp is used by both Algal Blend and slime production. Split or buffer it before processing. Growth often limits a farm before the Harvester's speed does. Everyday farms and food Egg collection: keep a small group of adult chickens above a hopper feeding a chest. The eggs are collected automatically; hatching and expanding the flock remain separate choices. Start with a few birds before adding more entities. Pumpkins and melons: a vanilla observer/piston lane can break the produced fruit while leaving the stem. Send drops toward a hopper collection path. Test the sensor direction with one plant first. Bone meal: feed compostable surplus such as seeds into a composter from above and extract bone meal below with hoppers. Keep planting stock first. The pack also offers renewable Limestone → Millstone → bone meal. Basic animals: start with manual breeding and a clear collection/storage routine for wool, milk or drops. A collector handles dropped items; it does not automatically breed or shear animals. Add automation only when the relevant machine and interaction are available. Food processing: reserve raw wheat for slime and planting supplies before milling surplus for food recipes. Choose smoking rather than a blasting airflow when the native food recipe calls for it. These small vanilla systems are useful before the workshop is large. A compact field and a visible buffer are easier to maintain than an oversized farm with no destination for its output. Renewable stone: foundation, drill, destination T&K3 changes lava/water stone generation using a foundation. The vertical order is generated stone → lens block → matching frame . The lens and frame stay in place. A generation event creates the selected stone; putting a lens below an existing rock does not convert that rock. Build a small normal lava/water generator with a safe collection cell. Under the intended stone cell, place the chosen lens, then the required frame one block further down. Use a powered Mechanical Drill pointing into the generated stone. Protect the lens and frame from the drill path. Collect the drops with a hopper or a belt/funnel route. Add storage before milling or crushing. Keep one output branch as building stone; send the material branch into the selected processor. The lens and frame are permanent foundation blocks, outside the breaking path. For earlier production, mill the metal stones into three nuggets. Nine nuggets make one ingot. Open all generator foundations · Explore processing recipes Fans: washing, haunting and safe outputs Put an Encased Fan behind the relevant processing medium and send its airflow across the items. Depots are a convenient first test; belts can carry a continuous line once the process works. Keep the washing and haunting lanes separate. Washing: fan → water → items. The pack includes sand → clay and washing for crushed geological metals. Haunting: fan → soul fire → items. At tier 4, Source Gem becomes Arcane Essence in this pack's recipe. Smoking / blasting: native Create fan processes use their respective heat medium. Look up the actual input before choosing the process, especially for food. Increasing fan RPM extends airflow reach; it does not directly reduce the processing time. If items pass too quickly, slow the belt, hold them on a depot, or extend their time in the airflow. Filter extraction so unprocessed inputs do not leave too early. Do not build an online iron or alloy farm merely because its layout looks familiar. T&K3 changes the material recipes. Follow the Crimsite route and the catalogue rather than assuming gravel-washing yields or the original Andesite Alloy recipe. Mechanism lines: one input, ordered hands All four mechanisms require sequenced assembly . Every sequence has one loop and one guaranteed output. The recipe viewer shows the actual order; the final tool belongs in the Deployer's hand , not on the belt. Your first Kinetic line Use a wooden slab as the belt input. Deploy one Andesite Alloy, deploy a second Andesite Alloy, then finish with a Deployer holding the BetterEnd Iron Hammer. The two alloys are separate operations. A reusable depot and one Deployer can demonstrate the steps by changing the held item. For continuous production, use an ordered line with separate supply points. Keep unfinished mechanisms travelling through every station; extract the finished mechanism at the end. Permanent workshop tools Chapters I–X award unbreakable finishing tools once per player. Make ordinary tools first so the reward never blocks the chapter's own production. Normal tools lose one durability per finish. The reward fits the same recipe and removes tool replacement from that station. Chapter V gives a second permanent Iron Hammer for a parallel Kinetic line. Automated frames then use casing → deploy one mechanism . Stonecut the resulting frame into the working machine. Keep casing production and mechanism assembly as separate supply lines; combine them at the frame station. Play the Kinetic walkthrough Slime and fluids: no pump needed for the first batch Tier 2 recipe: one kelp + one wheat + 250 mB water in a Basin under a Mixer → two slimeballs . No heat is required. Fill the first basin with a water bucket before you have pumps. For a continuous line, connect a water supply with the Hydraulic-tier fluid machines, keep kelp and wheat in separate buffers, and extract slimeballs without exporting the unprocessed inputs. Watch the basin: missing water, a stopped Mixer or the wrong crop item can each make the line appear stuck. A wheat mill produces flour, which is a different item and does not satisfy this slime recipe. Route raw wheat to slime before the remainder goes to food processing. Visualise the slime recipe Brass and smart logistics Tier 3: copper ingot + zinc ingot → heated Mixer → two brass ingots. Capture a blaze in a native Blaze Burner and supply fuel for the required heat. Mine the first zinc instead of waiting for an advanced renewable line. The Precision sequence uses a Sealed Mechanism, Brass Sheet and Electron Tube, then Create Sand Paper as the finishing tool. Precision frames open the smart logistics equipment. Add filters where outputs split, and reserve planting stock and reusable tools before exporting everything into general storage. For repeatable cutting, set the Saw's output filter. For multiple branches, plan a destination for every possible item and leave a visible buffer where problems can be spotted. Source and arcane automation Tier 4 adds magical processing to the mechanical workshop. Begin with the native Imbuement Chamber, Source Jars and available first-Source generators. Craft the bootstrap Agronomic Sourcelink from a Precision Machine, wheat, Source Gems and a Source Jar. Grow nearby crops to generate Source before the Arcane Machine. Make the Enchanting Apparatus from a Precision Machine, diamond and Source Gem. The visual recipe steps distinguish the central reagent from the pedestal ingredients and show the Source cost. Do not put all ingredients in the central block. Arcane Casing uses Brass Casing as reagent, Source Gem + Arcane Essence + gold on the pedestals, and 500 Source . Deploy an Arcane Mechanism onto that casing to make the Arcane Machine. Later apparatus recipes connect it to automation charms, source devices and Wizardry machinery. Store Source and ingredients before starting repeated recipes. An empty jar is not a full Source supply. Follow the pack's apparatus recipes for charms; native online recipes may differ. FE: extend the workshop, keep the early lines Tier 4 starts with two iron ingots + coal in a heated Mixer → two steel ingots. Build the Steel Casing using that steel, mined osmium and one Precision Machine. The first Heat Generator can be built before you already have FE. The Metallurgic Infuser is Steel Casing → deploy a Precision Mechanism . The mechanism is consumed; no boss catalyst or FE is required to build the first Infuser. Give the finished Infuser FE and the relevant native infusion material before processing. Enrichment turns the listed raw metals into two dust; native smelting makes two ingots. Keep steel, power and ore-refining branches buffered. AE2 starts in the same chapter with a Charger and Inscriber, followed by the Inductive Machine and small ME network. Chemistry and HDPE arrive in chapter 6. Basic chemical tanks, tubes, separator, PRC and rotary machine use Ender Machines so the HDPE line can run before the Chemical Machine. A reliable factory checklist Test one input and watch it reach the final storage. Check both the recipe unlock and the physical machine setup. Give every drop, by-product and unfinished item a destination. Keep tools, saplings, seeds and reusable catalysts out of blanket extraction. Leave a buffer before a slow or intermittent process. Stop or throttle production when storage fills; avoid piles of loose entities. Expand a working lane before adding several untested processes at once. On servers, build within the normal loaded area. Moving a machine or claiming a chunk does not by itself promise that it stays active while nobody is nearby. title: Engineering & storage
description: Connect Create production to Mekanism processing and an AE2 storage and autocrafting network.
text: Home / T&K3 / Engineering & storage Build & automate Engineering & storage Connect Create production to Mekanism processing and an AE2 storage and autocrafting network. ANDESITE → COPPER → BRASS → FE & ME → ENDER → CHEMICAL → SOVEREIGN. Create · build the backbone Start with a manual Kinetic Machine , then sequence mechanisms and deploy them onto casings. Earlier factories keep supplying the later layers. Slice & Dice connects Farmer’s Delight cutting and irrigation; Aquatic Ambitions connects copper fluid handling with ocean minerals and conduit processing. Hypertubes joins the brass logistics workshop. Chapter 4 · first FE and ME Bootstrap steel with heated mixing. Steel Casing and a Precision Mechanism make the first Metallurgic Infuser. Build a Heat Generator, cables, Charger and Inscriber before making the Inductive Mechanism . Crafts & Additions bridges rotational power and FE. AE2 starts with 1k storage, terminals, buses and processors ; the larger cells arrive later. Chapters 5–7 · factories and chemistry Chapter 5 opens the End and advanced factories. Chapter 6 introduces HDPE, hydrogen, chlorine, hydrogen chloride and Applied Mekanistics chemical cells . The first gas machines use an Ender Machine, so HDPE is reachable before the Chemical Machine. Chapter 7 treats Shadow Steel into Radiance and adds expedition airships, wireless access and 16k storage. Chapters 8–10 · containment and quantum production Containment enables fission, turbines and waste handling. Build the first SPS from Containment Frames in chapter 9, then use native antimatter processing to make Stargaze Singularities. Fusion, quantum links and 64k storage support the line. Chapter 10 finishes with 256k storage, powered equipment and the Sovereign Keystone. Storage that stays useful Sophisticated Storage & Backpacks provide early collection, filtering, processing and upgrades. Their native preserving recipes keep contents and components. The Create integration lets supported storage upgrades work on contraptions. ME chemical cell upgrades also preserve their stored chemicals. description: Track the new pack’s foundation and documented development changes.
text: Home / T&K3 / Changelog Project reference Changelog Track the new pack’s foundation and documented development changes. Living changelog for the rebuild of Towns & Kingdoms. Target: Minecraft 1.21.1 / NeoForge This page focuses on player/development-relevant changes between the T&K2 era and T&K3. The detailed working ledger is maintained in: TK3/docs/CHANGELOG_3.0.md Legacy reference T&K2 Mod List T&K2 — A New World | The 1.20.1 Update 3.0 — Rebuilt foundation Platform Moving to Minecraft 1.21.1 . Moving to NeoForge . T&K3 is a rebuild; T&K2 scripts/configs/assets are reference material instead of the runtime base. Progression FTB Quests becomes the visible campaign/progression layer. AStages enforces actual gameplay locks. End Remastered is integrated into End access. Boss kills and milestones can unlock reusable processing permissions/catalysts. Character progression A large Passive Skill Tree becomes the character progression foundation. Six main classes, eighteen subclasses and four professions form the current design. Combat Epic Fight is the core combat framework. Weapons of Miracles and Simply Swords are part of the selected weapon stack. T&K3 maintains compatibility/movesets for its own selected stack. Magic Iron's Spells focuses on combat spellcasting. Ars Nouveau focuses on arcane crafting, processing and automation. Just Another Witchery Remake joins the selected magic layer. Cross-mod recipes/progression intentionally connect the magic systems. Technology Create is the early/mid-game mechanical backbone. Mekanism becomes a later technology layer. AE2 becomes the late-game storage/logistics/autocrafting system. Create Aeronautics is integrated as a progression-based travel/engineering system. Compact automation is preferred over unnecessary multi-step processing bloat. Loot & gear Apotheosis / Apothic systems provide the affix, gem and socket framework. Default balance/progression is being customized for the pack. Bosses, mobs & exploration Selected 3.0 content currently includes Cataclysm, Alex's Mobs, Alex's Caves, Ice and Fire: Community Edition, Bosses' Rise, Mowzie's Mobs, Twilight Forest and Amplified Nether. Towns & multiplayer MineColonies is selected as the primary settlement/kingdom system for T&K3. MCA Reborn was only an early T&K3 consideration and was not part of T&K2. MineColonies: Epicfied (Epic Colonies) is now the primary MineColonies ↔ Epic Fight test candidate. Epic Fight X Minecolonies Compat remains the simpler fallback if Epic Colonies fails version or stability testing. The two Epic Fight bridge mods are never installed together. Create: MineColonies Link connects colony supply requests to Create logistics. Initial server limits target 100 citizens per colony, a 12-chunk colony radius, disabled colony force-loading, default pathfinding limits and a 40-raider cap. FTB Chunks + FTB Teams remain the current claims/team foundation. Additional integrations are evaluated for cross-mod value and server impact rather than mod count. Integration KubeJS, ProbeJS and LootJS form the scripting/integration base. Dedicated KubeJS integrations are locked for Create, Mekanism, Ars Nouveau, Iron's Spells and AE2. The pack is being designed around intentional cross-mod compatibility rather than isolated mod progression. Dungeons & structures The temporary definitive dungeon baseline is Integrated Dungeons & Structures, Integrated Dungeons Arise, Integrated Cataclysm, Integrated Stronghold, YUNG's Better Dungeons and Dungeons & Taverns. Large/Create-heavy structures will be made rarer where needed. Optimization & QoL The conservative optimization baseline now includes Sodium, Lithium, ModernFix, FerriteCore, ImmediatelyFast, Entity Culling, BadOptimizations, Dynamic FPS, AllTheLeaks, Clumps, FastSuite, spark and Chunky. The selected QoL baseline includes JEI, Jade, Jade Addons, AppleSkin, Mouse Tweaks, Controlling, Shulker Box Tooltip, Lootr, Iris and BetterF3. Explorer's Compass is intentionally excluded. Still in development final world generation economy expanded Towns & Kingdoms systems final version pins final Epic Fight compatibility coverage FreeTerraForged is now the primary Overworld terrain candidate, replacing ReTerraForged. The current Overworld test stack combines FreeTerraForged with Alex's Caves, Biomes O' Plenty, Oh The Biomes We've Gone, Upgrade Aquatic, Atmospheric, Autumnity, Environmental and [Let's Do] BloomingNature. The End test stack now uses BetterEnd: New Dawn as the primary overhaul, with Nullscape under terrain-layer testing. YUNG's Better End Island and End's Phantasm have been rejected to avoid unnecessary overlap. The Nether test stack now uses Amplified Nether + BetterNether: New Dawn + YUNG's Better Nether Fortresses. Gardens of the Dead has been rejected. Mod-by-mod comparison The detailed T&K2 → T&K3 comparison ledger is maintained in: TK3/docs/CHANGELOG_3.0.md As the definitive T&K3 mod list is completed, every meaningful T&K2 mod/system will be classified as Returning , Added , Replaced , Removed or Reworked . Official wiki · October 2026 The entire 2.0 and 3.0 wiki now lives in the official wiki on GitHub Pages. The visual workshop walks through the 1709 authored tier 1–10 recipes and one native Hopper Upgrade reference. The automation field guide explains collection, farms, processing, generators and common bottlenecks. Mechanisms use one-loop, deterministic sequenced assembly with mod tools; chapter milestones award unbreakable finishing tools. AStages provides actual gameplay locks so recipes, machines, items, equipment slots and major systems cannot be bypassed by gifting or finding late-game items. title: Legacy features
description: The original T&K2 features, including exploration, colonies, magic and automation.
text: Home / T&K2 / Legacy features T&K2 archive Legacy features The original T&K2 features, including exploration, colonies, magic and automation. Preserved T&K2 documentation. Recipes, platform and mod versions on this page belong to the legacy pack. Open the T&K3 wiki . ► Exploration Exploration in this modpack is a thrilling and diverse experience, enhanced by a combination of biome expansion, dungeon crawling, and an overhauled endgame. Biome Expansion The world generation is enriched by the inclusion of Biomes O' Plenty and Oh The Biomes You'll Go . These mods introduce a vast array of new biomes, each with unique landscapes, flora, and fauna. Whether you're traversing mystical forests, arid deserts, or vibrant meadows, these biomes add depth and variety to every exploration adventure. Caves The underground adventure is greatly enhanced with Alex's Caves , which introduces five new cave types that add complexity and interest to the mining experience. These new cave types make underground exploration more engaging and diverse. For more details, you can visit the Alex's Caves Wiki . Dungeons For adventurers seeking danger and treasure, the modpack includes both When Dungeons Arise and Integrated Dungeons and Structures . When Dungeons Arise adds massive, sprawling dungeons that challenge even the most seasoned players. These dungeons are filled with tough enemies, intricate layouts, and abundant rewards, offering a grand adventure for those brave enough to enter. Integrated Dungeons and Structures creates dungeons that seamlessly integrate with other mods like Create , Quark , Alex's Mobs , and Supplementaries . These dungeons are designed with complex machinery, unique mob encounters, and rich detail, making them a vital part of the exploration experience. Endgame Overhaul The journey to the End is no longer just about finding a stronghold and activating the portal. With End Remastered , the process becomes a grand adventure of its own. The End portal now requires 15 unique Eyes of Ender, each obtained through quests and challenges spread across the world. This change turns the quest for the End into a true test of exploration and endurance. Paired with Integrated Stronghold , the stronghold itself has been completely overhauled. The stronghold now features enhancements from mods like Create , Alex's Mobs , Quark , and Mowzie's Mobs . Expect intricate machinery, enhanced mob encounters, and the presence of powerful foes like the Wroughtnaut from Mowzie's Mobs. This makes the journey to the End not only longer but far more rewarding and challenging, culminating in a battle-ready stronghold that's as dangerous as it is awe-inspiring. ► Building Building in this modpack is a dream come true for creative players, offering a vast array of blocks and decorative options that cater to every architectural style. Modern Furniture MrCrayfish's Furniture Mod: Refurbished brings a modern touch to your builds with a wide range of contemporary furniture pieces, perfect for creating sleek, stylish interiors. Fantasy and Medieval Furniture Handcrafted adds a collection of fantasy and medieval-style furniture, providing the perfect accents for castles, fortresses, and rustic homes. Small Decorative Blocks Beautify offers small decorative blocks that add the finishing touches to your builds, enhancing the atmosphere of any space. Industrial and Mechanical Decor Create Deco integrates seamlessly with the Create mod, adding beautifully crafted, industrial-style decoration blocks that complement any mechanical build. Expanded Building Blocks Chipped dramatically expands your building palette with a plethora of new block variations, allowing for more detailed and creative designs. Natural Building Materials In addition to these mods, the world generation mods Better End , Better Nether , Oh The Biomes You'll Go (BYG) , Biomes O' Plenty (BOP) , and Regions Unexplored provide an extensive range of natural blocks and building materials, further expanding your creative possibilities. Summary Whether you're constructing a cozy cottage, a grand castle, or a futuristic factory, this modpack offers everything you need to bring your architectural visions to life. ► Mobs Mobs are made more diverse and interesting with mods like Alex's Mobs and Mowzie's Mobs , which introduce a wide range of new creatures with unique behaviors and abilities. Ice and Fire: Dragons adds mythical beasts that bring both challenge and reward. These mods together create a dynamic and unpredictable world where every encounter can be thrilling and dangerous. ► Quests The modpack comes with an extensive quest system, featuring over 1400 quests spread across 11 progression-based tabs, Exploration Tabs and More!. These quests cover various aspects of gameplay, including exploration, magic, technology, and more. The quests are designed to guide players through the modpack's content, providing rewards and goals that enhance the overall experience. ► MineColonies MineColonies is a key component of this modpack, giving players the tools to create and manage their own colonies. This mod allows you to recruit citizens, assign jobs, and build infrastructure, transforming a small settlement into a bustling town. The strategic elements of managing resources, expanding your colony, and defending against threats add depth and replayability to the gameplay. ► Magic Magic in this modpack is a rich and varied experience, offering players multiple paths to explore the mystical arts. Whether you prefer the structured spellcasting of Ars Nouveau , the dark, ritualistic power of Malum , the natural harmony of Botania , or the classic spellcraft of Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks , there's something here for every aspiring mage. Ars Nouveau lets you craft your own spells from the ground up, giving you the freedom to create magical solutions tailored to your needs. Whether you're conjuring fireballs, healing allies, or automating your base with magical constructs, Ars Nouveau provides the tools to turn your imagination into reality. For those who crave the darker side of magic, Malum offers a deep dive into the world of rituals and soul manipulation. Harness the power of the spirits, perform complex rituals, and unlock abilities that blur the line between life and death. Malum's magic is not for the faint of heart, but for those willing to embrace the shadows, it offers unparalleled power. Botania , on the other hand, is all about the synergy between magic and nature. This mod allows you to tap into the natural world to generate mana, which can then be used to craft powerful tools, gear, and gadgets. From creating beautiful, functional gardens to wielding mana-infused weapons, Botania makes you feel like a true nature mage. Finally, Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks adds a classic touch to the magical lineup. With wands, spellbooks, and a wide variety of spells to learn and master, this mod brings a more traditional magic experience into the mix. Whether you're summoning familiars, casting elemental spells, or teleporting across the world, Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks will make you feel like you're attending your own personal wizarding school. With these powerful mods at your disposal, magic becomes a central element of your journey through the world, offering endless possibilities for creativity, power, and discovery. ► Combat The Epic Fight mod transforms Minecraft's combat system into a more dynamic and visually engaging experience, reminiscent of action RPGs. This mod replaces the standard combat mechanics with a system that emphasizes timing, movement, and weapon variety, making every battle feel more intense and strategic. How It Works Epic Fight overhauls the way combat functions in Minecraft by introducing new animations, attack styles, and a dedicated combat mode. When combat mode is active, your character will perform different actions based on the type of weapon you're wielding, whether it’s a sword, axe, or even bare fists. Key Features Combat Mode Toggle (R) : To switch between building and combat modes, simply press the R key. In combat mode, your character's movement and actions change to fit the more dynamic combat system. For instance, sprinting becomes a dodge roll, and standard attacks become combos and power strikes. Weapon-Specific Animations : Each weapon type comes with its own set of animations and attack patterns. For example, wielding a sword allows you to perform quick slashes, while an axe delivers slower but more powerful strikes. The mod also supports shields, bows, and other weapons, each with its own unique combat style. Weapon Types The Epic Fight mod supports a wide variety of weapon types, each with unique animations and combat styles. The available weapon types in the modpack include: Swords Katanas Tachis Spears Battlestaffs Daggers Axes Greatswords Shields Tridents Bows Crossbows Mod Integration and Custom Support This modpack comes with full custom support for Epic Fight, seamlessly integrating it with every weapon in the game. In addition to vanilla weapons, the modpack specifically supports weapons from the following mods: Simply Swords Knaves' Needs L'Ender's Cataclysm The Aether Twilight Forest Deeper & Darker Applied Energistics 2 (AE2) Better Nether Better End Farmer's Delight Ice & Fire: Dragons Alex's Caves Iron's Spells 'n Spellbooks Botania Ars Nouveau Malum Mowzie's Mobs ► The Skill Tree The Passive Skilltree Mod in this modpack introduces a deep and customizable skill tree, inspired by the complex and rewarding systems found in games like Path of Exile. This mod allows players to tailor their character's abilities to fit their preferred playstyle. To gain skill points, the modpack features a custom-made item called the Skill Point Scroll . These scrolls can be obtained randomly through quests, adding an element of surprise and reward as you progress. Additionally, defeating bosses guarantees a Skill Point Scroll drop, ensuring that your most challenging victories are always rewarded with a chance to further enhance your character's capabilities. If you ever want to reset your skill tree, the modpack also includes a custom-made Reset Scroll . This scroll can also be obtained through questing, providing flexibility and allowing you to reallocate your skill points as you see fit. To access the skill tree, simply press the "O" key, and you'll be able to navigate the extensive array of skills available. With over 300 different skill points to choose from, the Passive Skilltree Mod allows for a highly personalized and strategic approach to character development, making every choice and point allocation meaningful. ► Automation Automation in this modpack is a central theme, driven by the incredible versatility of the Create mod. The entire progression system is built around 11 tiers of custom recipes, meticulously designed to integrate Create with other major mods like Thermal Expansion , Applied Energistics 2 , and more. Thanks to KubeJS , over 500 custom recipes have been crafted to ensure a seamless integration of Create with these mods, enhancing your automation capabilities at every tier. As you progress, you’ll unlock increasingly complex machines and automation setups, making use of different Create addons like Create Crafts & Additions and The Factory Must Grow (TFMG) . The Factory Must Grow (TFMG) adds new layers to the automation process by introducing oil and advanced steel production mechanics, further expanding the industrial capabilities of your setups. These additions allow for more complex production chains and higher-level machinery, making automation more intricate and rewarding. From basic contraptions to intricate production lines, the possibilities are nearly endless. By the time you reach the final tiers, you’ll be able to automate almost everything in the game, from resource gathering and processing to complex crafting sequences. Whether you're looking to streamline your mining operations or automate the production of high-tech machinery, this modpack's automation system provides all the tools you need to turn your factory dreams into reality. text: Home / T&K2 / A New World · legacy update T&K2 archive A New World · legacy update The original 1.20.1 update and its eleven-chapter direction. Preserved T&K2 documentation. Recipes, platform and mod versions on this page belong to the legacy pack. Open the T&K3 wiki . 1.20.1 "A New World" Update The 1.20.1 "A New World" update marks a complete rework of the modpack, evolving from its previous 1.18.2 version to introduce a wealth of new content and improvements. This ambitious update has been over a year in the making, expanding the modpack from its original 7 chapters to 11 chapters of progression, offering players more depth, challenges, and rewards as they journey through the modded world. Major Changes and Additions 500 Recipe Changes : The update includes a comprehensive overhaul of the crafting system, with around 500 recipes being reworked to better integrate with the new and existing mods. This ensures a more cohesive and balanced gameplay experience that enhances the progression and crafting aspects of the modpack. 1400 New Quests : To guide players through the expanded content, 1400 new quests have been added. These quests are designed to not only introduce the new features and mods but also provide a structured progression that keeps the gameplay engaging and rewarding from start to finish. New Mods and Removals : As part of the rework, several mods have been removed to improve stability and performance, while many new mods have been added to bring fresh features and fun to the modpack. This careful curation of mods ensures that the pack is more streamlined and enjoyable than ever before. Major Mod Changes The 1.20.1 "A New World" update brings significant changes to the mod lineup, ensuring the pack remains streamlined, balanced, and fully compatible with the latest Minecraft version. Here are some of the key changes: Removed Mods : Industrial Foregoing : Removed as it didn't fit the theme of the pack and wasn't a good addition overall. Immersive Engineering & Immersive Petroleum : These mods have been replaced by Create: The Factory Must Grow , which aligns better with the modpack's focus and provides a more cohesive experience. Buzzier Bees, Autumnity, Atmospheric : These mods were removed due to their unavailability on 1.20.1. Beyond Earth : Replaced with Ad Astra , offering a more refined space exploration experience. Blood Magic : Removed as it no longer fits within the theme and balance of the modpack. Hex Casting : Also removed due to thematic inconsistencies. Blue Skies : Replaced with the Aether Mod , which better suits the overall feel of the pack. Backpacked, Functional Storage, Iron Chests : These storage mods have been replaced by Sophisticated Backpacks & Storage , offering a more unified and feature-rich storage solution. Tinkers' Construct : Unfortunately, due to a lack of updates for 1.20.1, Tinkers' Construct has been removed from the pack. Psi : Removed for the same reason as Tinkers' Construct, due to it not being updated for 1.20.1. Pam's HarvestCraft : Removed due to outdated textures and features that no longer align with the visual and functional standards of the modpack. Added Mods : Let's Do Mod Series : This series has been added to introduce new crops, blocks, and features like wine making, brewing beer, and much more, enriching the farming and crafting aspects of the modpack. Apotheosis : Reintroduced with significant nerfs to ensure a balanced and enjoyable experience that fits within the modpack's progression. Simply Swords : Hundreds of new weapons have been added, with Knaves' Needs providing compatibility for mods like Twilight Forest, BetterEnd, and Better Nether, expanding combat options. Iron's Spells & Spellbooks : This new magic mod allows players to create spellbooks with unique spells for both utility and combat, offering a fresh magical experience. Alex's Caves : Adds massive caves with unique biomes and mobs, enhancing the underground exploration aspect of the game. Passive Skilltree : This mod introduces a skill tree system with over 300 different skill points, allowing players to build their own unique playstyle. Choose from Armorer skills for increased durability or Hunter skills for more damage, among many other options. Improved Stability and Features With the "A New World" update, players can expect not only more content but also a smoother, more stable experience. The update has been optimized to reduce crashes and improve overall performance, making it easier to dive into the complex world of mods without interruptions. Ongoing Support The 1.20.1 update also marks the beginning of more active updates and patches. The modpack will receive regular support, ensuring that bugs are promptly addressed, new features are added, and the community’s feedback is incorporated into future updates. text: Home / T&K2 / Legacy server installation T&K2 archive Legacy server installation The original server instructions. Check the legacy pack and platform before following them. Preserved T&K2 documentation. Recipes, platform and mod versions on this page belong to the legacy pack. Open the T&K3 wiki . You need Java 21 to host 1.20.1 modpacks. Download the Serverpack Navigate to the Curseforge page for the version you wish to play. Go to the Files tab and click the latest file. Navigate to Additional Files and download the serverpack files. Running Your Server Before anything, make sure you've extracted the initial serverpack file you downloaded! Windows If you see a startserver.bat file in the serverpack, double-click it to run your server. macOS Open the Terminal app (found in /Applications/Utilities/ ). Type cd <path_to_installer> and press Enter to navigate to the installation folder. Replace <path_to_installer> with the actual path. If you don't know the path, type cd (with a space) and drag the installer folder into the Terminal. Run the following commands: chmod +x ./startserver.sh (this makes the script executable). ./startserver.sh (to run the installation script). Linux Ensure curl is installed (if using Ubuntu, you may need to install wget to get curl ). Navigate to the modpack directory and make the script executable: chmod +x startserver.sh Start the modpack with: ./startserver.sh Common Questions How do I join my server? Install the modpack using a modded launcher (e.g., Curseforge, ATLauncher). Go to the Multiplayer tab in Minecraft. Click Direct Connect and type localhost . How do others join my server? They will connect using your Public IP Address. Find it by typing "my ip address" in Google. If they can't join, look up a port forwarding guide online. How do I allocate more RAM? Open the user_jvm_args.txt file. Cahge the Java arguments within the quotation marks. For example, -Xmx8g will set maximum RAM usage to 8GB. Should I be worried about errors in the console? Unless something isn't working as expected, most errors (99%) mean nothing important. Why is my server so laggy? Follow this guide for optimal Java arguments (note: these can cause instability for some users). If lag persists, use this in-game command: /spark profiler start --only-ticks-over 50 . Check the Spark Profiler link in chat/console and verify if your server is using all available memory. You can allocate more memory or check resource usage in the Spark Profiler. Ask for help in the Discord if needed. How do I make my server public? To get your server listed in the Server Browser , click the Add Server button in the Multiplayer menu. Servers hosted with Bisect get higher placement on the server list. Make sure to post under the correct modpack. Alternative to Self Hosting If you'd prefer a hosted solution, consider using Bisect for server hosting: Prices range from $10 to $25 per month (depending on the plan). Use code Mika for 25% off. We suggest choosing at least 1GB per player (minimum 4GB for server stability). You can order a plan here .
